subject: Stalled close: request for MAP heat-check and reprofile
messages:
From: Elaine Wu <elaine@newton.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit@newton.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Close timeline concern — MAP status and contingency ask

Markus,

Thanks for running the workshop last week. We got internal alignment on the evaluation scope, but two issues cropped up during our internal perf runs: (1) latency variance on tail loads is exceeding our SLOs, and (2) the integration with our tokenization wrapper is flakier than expected when we push batched traffic.

At this point the executive team is asking for a realistic rebaseline — we were targeting go-live 2026-12-15 but we need a clear mutual action plan (MAP) that sequences remaining gating items and shows acceptable contingency options. Can you send a heat-check of the MAP and a short list of mitigations? We may need to pause the current sales milestone if there's no feasible short-term fix.

Attachments: Newton_MAP_v3.xlsx (latest MAP we walked through), performance_snapshot_20261130.pdf

What we'd find most useful from Redwood: recommended short-list of actions for the next two weeks, an updated risk register with owners, and a clear fallback if dedicated capacity isn't available.

Appreciate a candid assessment — Elaine
Elaine Wu
Head of ML Platform 
Newton Systems

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine@newton.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit@newton.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Close timeline concern — MAP status and contingency ask

Elaine — thanks for the note and for the attachments. Short answer: we can produce a two-week tactical MAP with concrete owners and a fallback lane, but there will be trade-offs (latency vs cost and a short period of elevated monitoring).

Next steps I'll take today:
- Pull the runbook and current infra config; validate whether your tokenization wrapper mismatch is a config or SDK edge case (owner: Markus).
- Ask Product & SRE for a prioritized short fixes list (owner: Laura Bennett).
- Prepare a contingency lane outlining: 1) temporary dedicated capacity bump, 2) aggressive KV-prefix caching for the hot paths, 3) roll-forward with quantized model if accuracy tests pass (owner: Grace O'Connor).

I expect to deliver a revised MAP (two-week tactical) and a compact risk log by EOD tomorrow. If we see kernel-level perf degradation we'll request a short SLA exception window to test on dedicated nodes.

I'll copy internal stakeholders and loop in procurement if we need to accelerate a dedicated pool.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: markus@redwood.ai, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: quick sync — Newton MAP heat-check and risk catalog

Team — pulling a quick internal triage together before we send the external note. Notes from my review of the artifacts:

Quick findings
- Perf snapshot shows ~3x tail latency on 512-token batched requests under spike profile vs baseline. Likely contributors: tokenization mismatch + KV cache warm-up pattern.
- Integration tests fail intermittently when the client's token wrapper returns varying encodings for stray UTF-8 sequences.

Immediate mitigations (48–72h):
1) Tokenization shim: ship a small compatibility shim (Priyom) that normalizes encodings and falls back to our tokenizer for odd cases. Impact: medium dev effort, low infra risk.
2) Prefix KV priming: detect hot prefixes in the first 5k calls and prefill KV cache on dedicated nodes (Grace). Impact: ops change, quick perf wins for steady-state.
3) Temporary dedicated bump: 2x capacity for one week to reduce queuing latency while we stabilize (needs procurement signoff).
4) Telemetry gating: add a focused eval harness against spike patterns and snapshot before/after changes (Laura + Grace).

Risk register draft (for Newton MAP v3)
- Risk A: Token wrapper variability -> owner: Priyom -> mitigation: shim + test vectors -> residual: medium
- Risk B: Kernel path on long sequences -> owner: Grace -> mitigation: run targeted kernel profile, consider shorter chunking -> residual: medium-high
- Risk C: Procurement lead time for dedicated nodes -> owner: Markus -> mitigation: prepare purchase path and fallback to hosted burst where possible -> residual: medium

Deliverables for external update
- 2-week tactical MAP with owners and dates
- Compact risk register (3–5 rows)
- One-page contingency options with estimated cost delta

I'll assemble the MAP and risk table this morning and send to Markus for sign-off. Priyom / Grace — can you confirm owners and estimate ETA for their tasks (hours)?

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine@newton.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit@newton.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, procurement <procurement@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 14:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Stalled close: request for MAP heat-check and reprofile — compact plan

Elaine — attached is a short tactical MAP and the draft risk catalog. High-level summary below and next actions.

High-level reprofile
- Original target: 2026-12-15 go-live
- New tactical target window for go/no-go decision: 2026-12-18 to 2026-12-22 (decision gate on 2026-12-22).

What we will deliver (next 10 business days)
1) Tokenization shim (owner: Priyom) — ETA: 48–72 hours. Purpose: eliminate encoding variance causing intermittent regression.
2) Prefix KV priming on dedicated nodes (owner: Grace) — ETA: 72 hours to enable + 24 hours monitoring.
3) Short-term dedicated capacity bump (owner: Markus / procurement) — procurement to confirm same-day order path; fallback: hosted burst for 72 hours.
4) Focused perf harness and acceptance run (owner: Laura) — run before and after each mitigation, send snapshot results.

Escalation note
If the decision gate on 2026-12-22 shows unacceptable tail latency: we recommend pausing public rollout and move to a phased canary with restricted traffic plus extended monitoring (30-day extended burn) while we complete kernel-level profiling and potential model quantization trials.

Attachments: Newton_MAP_v3_reprofile.xlsx (two-week tactical), newton_risk_catalog_20261202.csv, performance_snapshot_20261130.pdf

Please confirm that the decision gate date works for Newton's execs and whether you'd like Redwood to open a procurement ticket for a dedicated pool immediately. We'll treat the procurement path as an expedited approval if you request.

Thanks — Markus
Markus Klein
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
